questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution provides for a bicameral Parliament of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 79**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Article 79 of the Indian Constitution does indeed establish the bicameral nature of the Indian Parliament.
 
 
• The Indian Parliament is a bicameral legislature which consists of two houses: the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) and the Lok Sabha (House of the People), along with the President of India.
 
• The President has the power to summon and preside over the sessions of both the houses, and he or she can also dissolve the Lok Sabha.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **Article 80**: This Article states that the Rajya Sabha will consist of not more than 250 members. Out of these, 12 are nominated by the President from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in the fields of literature, science, art, and social service, and the rest represent the States and Union territories.
 
• **Article 81**: This Article provides for the composition of the Lok Sabha. The House of the People or Lok Sabha consists of representatives directly elected by people of the territorial constituencies in the states and Union territories. As per the amendment of 1977, the Lok Sabha shall consist of not more than 552 members - up to 530 members to represent the territorial constituencies in the States, up to 20 members from Union Territories.
 
• **Article 83**: It determines the duration of the Houses of Parliament. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body and not subject to dissolution. However, Lok Sabha is elected for five years but can be dissolved earlier by the President.
 
• **Article 85**: Gives the President the right to summon each House at such intervals that there shouldn't be more than six months gap between the two sessions. Hence the parliament must meet at least twice a year.
 
• **Article 86**: Gives the President the right to address and send messages to either House of Parliament.

The Constitution of India therefore, in its Articles 79 to 122, provides detailed provisions for the organization, composition, duration, officers, procedures, privileges, and so on for the Parliament in India. The Parliament plays a critical role in the Indian democracy and has substantial legislative, executive, and financial powers. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 49**: This Article falls under the DPSP section of the Constitution. It states that it shall be the obligation of the State to protect every monument or place or object of artistic or historic interest, declared by or under law made by Parliament to be of national importance, from spoliation, disfigurement, destruction, removal, disposal or export, as the case may be.
 
• **Article 59**: This Article deals with the conditions of the President's office. It states that the President shall not be a member of either house of the Parliament or of a house of the legislature of any State, and if any such member is elected President, they shall be deemed to have vacated their seat in that house on the date on which they enter upon their office as President. Additionally, the President shall not hold any other office of profit.
 
• **Article 89**: Article 89 of the Constitution discusses the Deputy Chairman of the Council of States, or the Rajya Sabha (Upper House). It states that the council of states will choose one of its members to be the Deputy Chairman whenever the position becomes vacant, and the chosen member will perform the duties of the Chairman when the position of Chairman is vacant or when the Vice-President is acting as, or discharging the functions of, the President.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 153**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 153** of the Indian Constitution mentions that a person may be appointed as the Governor of two or more states.
 
• This provision allows for administrative convenience and efficiency in the governance of states.
 
• The appointment of the Governor is done by the President of India.
 
• In cases where a single individual is appointed as the Governor of multiple states, the individual exercises the powers and functions of the Governor in each of those states separately.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
 
• The Union List has been amended several times to meet the evolving needs of the nation.

questions.question: Who among the following can issue ordinance when the state legislature is not in session and he is satisfied that immediate action is required?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Ordinance-making power of the Governor is his most important legislative power.
 
• He can promulgate ordinances when the state legislature is not in session.
 
• In the case of a bicameral legislature, he can promulgate an ordinance even when one house is not in session.
 
• These ordinances must be approved by the state legislature within six weeks of their reassembly.
 
• He can also withdraw an ordinance at any time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• Governor:

 
 
• The Constitution of India envisages the same pattern of government in the states as that for the Centre, that is, a parliamentary system.
 
• Part VI of the Constitution deals with the government in the states.
 
• Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Constitution deal with the state executive.
 
• The state executive consists of the governor, the chief minister, the council of ministers, and the advocate general of the state.
 
• Thus, there is no office of the vice-governor (in the state) like that of the Vice-President at the Centre.
 
• The governor is the chief executive head of the state.
 
• But, like the president, he is a nominal executive head (titular or constitutional head). 
 
• The governor also acts as an agent of the central government. 
 
• Therefore, the office of the governor has a dual role.
 
• Usually, there is a governor for each state, but the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1956 facilitated the appointment of the same person as a governor for two or more states.

questions.question: Who advises the Governor with respect to proroguing of the session of the State Legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chief Minister**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Chief Minister advises the Governor on proroguing the session of the State Legislature.
 
• Proroguing refers to the ending of a session of the legislature, after which a new session may be convened.
 
• This advice is given by the Chief Minister as part of their executive role in the state government.
 
• The Governor acts on this advice in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **State Legislature:**

 
 
• The State Legislature consists of the Governor and one or two houses, as per the state's constitution.
 
• In states with bicameral legislatures, there is a Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).
 
 
 
• **Governor:**
 
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state, appointed by the President of India.
 
• The Governor's role includes summoning, proroguing, and dissolving the State Legislature on the advice of the Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Proroguing:**
 
 
• Proroguing is the termination of a session of the legislature without dissolving it.
 
• It results in the adjournment of all pending legislative business until the next session.
 
 
 
• **Executive Role of Chief Minister:**
 
 
• The Chief Minister is the head of the state government and leads the Council of Ministers.
 
• The Chief Minister advises the Governor on various matters, including legislative sessions, state policy, and administration.

questions.question: As per Article 172(2) ______ of a State shall NOT be subject to dissolution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Legislative Council**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 
 
**Article 172(2) of the Constitution of India states:-**

 
 
• 
 
**"A member holding office as a member of an Assembly shall, unless the Assembly is sooner dissolved, continue to hold office until immediately before the first meeting of the Assembly elected next after the dissolution of the Assembly." **

 
 
 
 
• **Composition of the Legislative Councils : **
 
 
• Article 169 of the Constitution allows Parliament to either create or abolish a Legislative Council in a state if the Legislative Assembly of the State passes a resolution to that effect.
 
• The total number of *members in the Legislative Council of a State having such a Council shall not exceed one-third *of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that State.
 
• The total number of members in the Legislative Council of a State shall in no case be less than 40.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Legislative Assembly:-**

 
 
• It is an institution of representative democracy where elected representatives, usually known as Members of the Legislative Assembly (MLAs), meet to debate and create legislation.
 
• These assemblies are part of the legislative process, particularly in parliamentary governments, and are often the lower house in the bicameral legislative structure common to many countries.
 
 
 
• **House of People:-**
 
 
• In the Indian context refers to the Lok Sabha, which is the lower house of India's bicameral Parliament.
 
• The members of the Lok Sabha are elected by the Indian public in general elections, which take place every five years.
 
 
 
• **Council of States:-**
 
 
• It refers to the Rajya Sabha, which is the upper house of the Parliament of India.
 
• The name "Rajya Sabha" translates to "Council of States" in English, signifying its role in representing the various states and union territories of India.

questions.question: As per Article 163 of the Constitution of India, any advice tendered by Ministers to the _______ shall not be inquired into in any court.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 163 of the Constitution of India pertains to the Council of Ministers advising the Governor of a state.
 
• The Governor is the constitutional head of the state, and the real executive authority lies with the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• According to Article 163(3), the question of whether any, and if so what, advice was tendered by Ministers to the Governor shall not be inquired into in any court.
 
• This provision is meant to preserve the confidentiality of the advice given by the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
 
• The Governor acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers except in cases where he/she is required to act in his/her discretion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Governor's Role**

 
 
• The Governor is appointed by the President of India and holds office at the President's pleasure.
 
• The Governor's powers include legislative powers, executive powers, financial powers, and judicial powers.
 
• The Governor has the power to summon, prorogue, and dissolve the state legislature.
 
• In certain situations, the Governor can act independently, such as in the appointment of the Chief Minister when there is no clear majority.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Chief Minister, aids and advises the Governor in the exercise of his/her functions.
 
• It is collectively responsible to the legislative assembly of the state.
 
• The Council of Ministers is instrumental in policy formulation and administration of the state.
 
 
 
• **Discretionary Powers of the Governor**
 
 
• Discretionary powers are exercised by the Governor without the advice of the Council of Ministers.
 
• These powers include reserving a bill for the President's consideration, recommending President's Rule, and seeking information from the Chief Minister regarding the legislative and administrative matters of the state.
 
• The Governor also has the discretion to appoint the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority in the legislative assembly.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Immunity**
 
 
• Article 163(3) ensures judicial immunity to the advice given by the Council of Ministers to the Governor.
 
• This immunity is designed to maintain the confidentiality and integrity of the executive advice process.

questions.question: The Governor of an Indian state before entering upon his office takes an oath or affirmation before _______.

options.text: the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State
the Chief Minister of the concerned state

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the Chief Justice of the High Court exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor of an Indian state** is appointed by the** President of India** and holds the office during the** pleasure of the President.**
 
• Before entering upon his office, the Governor takes an** oath or affirmation** before the** Chief Justice of the High Court** exercising jurisdiction in relation to the State.
 
• The purpose of taking the oath or affirmation is to ensure that the Governor will **faithfully discharge the duties **of his office and uphold the **Constitution and the laws** of the land.
 
• The oath or affirmation is a solemn promise made by the Governor to fulfill his** obligations with honesty, integrity, and dedication.**
 
• The Chief Justice of the High Court administering the oath or affirmation is a symbol of the** independence of the judiciary** and the **rule of law.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The **Chief Minister **is the **head of the state government** and has no role in the appointment or swearing-in of the Governor.
 
• The **Prime Minister** is the** head of the central government **and has no role in the appointment or swearing-in of the Governor.

questions.question: What is the duration for which a member of a House of Legislature of a State is, without permission of the House, absent from all meetings, thereof the house may declare his seat vacant?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**60 days**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A member of the House of Legislature of a State may lose their seat if they are absent from all meetings of the House for **60 days without its permission**.
 
• This provision is governed by **Article 190(4)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The absence is calculated continuously, excluding any period when the House is prorogued or adjourned for more than four consecutive days.
 
• The House must declare the seat vacant through a formal resolution or process to enforce this provision.
 
• The rule ensures **accountability of legislators** and prevents misuse of privileges by absenteeism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 190 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It deals with the **vacation of seats, disqualification, and resignation** of members of the State Legislature.
 
• Clause (4) specifies the conditions under which a seat becomes vacant due to prolonged absenteeism.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Speaker:**
 
 
• The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly or the Chairman of the Legislative Council decides on matters related to absenteeism and seat vacancy.
 
• The decision must follow the procedures laid out in the House Rules.
 
 
 
• **Prorogation and Adjournment:**
 
 
• Prorogation refers to the formal ending of a legislative session by the Governor.
 
• Adjournment refers to the suspension of a meeting of the House for a specific period.
 
• Absenteeism during prorogation or long adjournments is not counted towards the 60-day rule.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of the Provision:**
 
 
• The provision ensures that legislators remain **committed to their responsibilities** and participate in legislative processes.
 
• It prevents wastage of public resources due to non-participation by elected representatives.

questions.question: The Legislative Council of a state assembly __________ of the total number of members in the legislative of the state and in no case fewer than 40 members.
questions.solution:

__

• **Article 361** makes it clear that any court, tribunal or entity appointed or appointed by any House of Parliament to investigate a complaint pursuant to Article 61 can bring the President's conduct under investigation.
 
• Any criminal proceedings cannot be started or continued in any court during its term of office against the President, or the Governor of a State.

• Manik Saha was appointed as the chief minister of Tripura on **10 March 2022,** following the resignation of the previous chief minister **Biplab Kumar Deb.**
 
• The by-election in the Town Bardowali constituency was held after the resignation of the sitting MLA, **Sudip Roy Barman,** who joined the BJP after leaving the Trinamool Congress.
 
• The Tripura Legislative Assembly has a total of** 60 seats**, out of which 59 are elected and one is nominated.
 
• The current ruling party in Tripura is the **BJP, **which won a majority in the 2018 assembly elections by winning **36 out of 60 seats.**
